elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: After deletion of the reversal carve-out the clause reads "...(\"DEVELOPMENTS\"), shall be owned by Corio, including intellectual property rights in the Developments." Ownership of the Developments now vests unconditionally in Corio (Customer), with no support-triggered reversion to Commerce One.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained: "To the extent that Commerce One would otherwise have a claim of ownership in such Developments, Commerce One hereby assigns all rights in and to such Developments to Corio." Present-tense assignment from Vendor to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained opening words: "Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio" — Vendor's pre-existing IP is expressly carved out of the Customer ownership grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Added: "Commerce One grants Corio a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use any Commerce One intellectual property embedded in the Developments."

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence expressly states the licence is "irrevocable".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence expressly states the licence is "royalty-free".

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Added: "Corio retains all right, title and interest in all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers" — covers every category of Customer data, not selected named types.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Added: "any Commerce One license in such data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the Software, the MarketSite.net Service and Maintenance and Support under this Agreement." The enumerated purposes are service delivery only; no distribution, resale or independent-exploitation right and no "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" catch-all remains.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Added proviso to the final sentence: "...shall be negotiated by the parties prior to the start of any such development work, provided that no intellectual property shall be jointly owned by the parties." The retained negotiation mechanic survives without contradiction (the parties must negotiate sole ownership).

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: "Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio" preserves Vendor ownership of its pre-existing materials and technology; nothing in the edits divests Vendor of its generic tools or know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Customer's position exceeds a licence: Developments "shall be owned by Corio" and Commerce One "hereby assigns all rights in and to such Developments to Corio" — outright unconditional ownership subsumes a perpetual licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: An unconditional present assignment of "all rights in and to such Developments" with the support-triggered reversion deleted leaves nothing revocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The assignment of "all rights in and to such Developments" and Corio ownership carry no territorial limitation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Ownership/assignment is granted without any royalty, fee or payment condition in Section 13.5.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As owner of the Developments ("shall be owned by Corio"), Corio's use and modification rights are unrestricted; no field-of-use or use restriction is retained in the clause.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership plus the assignment of "all rights" includes the right to sublicense; the only restriction retained runs against Corio's disclosure of Commerce One proprietary information, not against exploitation of the Developments.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence limits any Commerce One licence in Corio data to "processing that data solely to provide the Software, the MarketSite.net Service and Maintenance and Support under this Agreement."

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the ownership-reversal carve-out is deleted so Developments vest unconditionally in Corio, the existing Commerce One assignment and pre-existing IP reservation are retained, and the three added terms supply the embedded-IP licence (perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free), Customer data ownership with a service-delivery-only Vendor processing limit, and an express no-joint-ownership proviso.
The walk-away trigger is cured: no residual sentence assigns Corio IP or Corio data to Commerce One; the support-based reversion of ownership is removed rather than merely qualified.

Fallback also reads as satisfied because outright Customer ownership plus the retained Vendor assignment subsumes the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense licence, and Vendor's pre-existing materials and technology ownership is preserved.

Minimality holds: exactly three operations, each traceable to a checklist element (delete the reversal for Customer ownership; add the embedded-IP licence and data-ownership/processing-limit sentence; add the no-joint-ownership proviso). No survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, indemnity or other model-language extra is imported, and no Customer-favourable retained wording is removed.

Intent is preserved: the redlined sentence remains grammatical ("shall be owned by Corio, including intellectual property rights in the Developments"), the Employee NDA/Invention Agreement covenants, Corio's non-disclosure covenant and the negotiation mechanic for Software enhancements all survive; the no-joint-ownership proviso narrows but does not contradict that negotiation mechanic, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting nit only (not a defect requiring repair): the data sentence covers "Corio or its Customers" — confirm this tracks any defined data terms used elsewhere in the Agreement so the new sentence and the MarketSite.net Service terms do not diverge.
